stories.title: Bachi the leafcutter ant
stories.intro: Today you're a worker leafcutter ant.

n1.text: You're Bachi, a worker leafcutter ant. Today you leave the nest with your line for the first time. Time to find leaves for the garden!

choices.text: Go off on my own another way

n1b.text: You wander from the line and everything is huge… you can't find your way back! But your antennae pick up the scent your sisters leave on the ground: it's their map.

n2.text: You reach a mango tree with tender leaves. What do you do?

choices.text: Cut a little piece with my jaws

n3.text: You're carrying a piece of leaf bigger than you. On the way, a raindrop falls right next to you. What do you do?

choices.text: Keep going with the line, slowly

n3b.text: You run… and a sister picks up your leaf. In the line, nobody works alone. You go back to help her.

n4.text: You reach the nest. Some tiny ants, the gardeners, chew the leaf and give it to the fungus. What now?

e_learn.text: Yuck! Leafcutter ants can't eat leaves. Leaves are for feeding the fungus in the nest, and the fungus is our food.

e_happy.text: Delicious! Thanks to everyone's work, the fungus grows and the colony eats. Leafcutter ants have been farmers for millions of years.

e_happy2.text: What a hard worker! A colony can have millions of sisters. Together they move lots of soil, and that lets air into the ground.

stories.title: Lita the angelita bee
stories.intro: Today you're a little stingless bee.

n1.text: You're Lita, a tiny angelita bee. You live in a hollow tree with an entrance like a little wax tube. Today it's your turn to find nectar.

choices.text: Go to the hibiscus in the yard
Go to a soda cup someone left

n2.text: There's a girl watching you at the hibiscus. What do you do?

n2b.text: You hide behind a petal… but the girl just watches, without touching. She's a forest ranger! You go back to the flower.

n3.text: Your back legs fill up with pollen, like little yellow baskets. When you visit another flower, the pollen travels with you and helps it make seeds.

n4.text: At the entrance, the guards check you. If an intruder came, they'd tangle in its hair and nibble it: their stinger is too tiny to work.

choices.text: Go in and store the nectar

e_learn.text: Soda is sweet, but it isn't nectar: it doesn't have what you need, and the flowers miss your visit. They need you to make seeds!

e_happy.text: You store the nectar in little wax pots, where it will turn into honey. In Venezuela, angelita honey has been treasured for a long time. And the hibiscus will make seeds!

e_happy2.text: Now you're a guard. Angelita bees take turns: some guard the door and others go out to the flowers. Teamwork is their superpower.

stories.title: A firefly night
stories.intro: Today you're a click beetle firefly from the plains.

n1.text: You're a click beetle firefly. You spent the day hiding under tree bark. Night falls on the plains. Time to switch on your lanterns!

choices.text: Switch on my two green lights

n1b.text: In the dark nobody sees you… not even the other fireflies you're looking for. For fireflies, light is how they talk.

n2.text: You fly with your green lights. Below you see some kids with a jar. What do you do?

choices.text: Fly high, away from the jar

n2b.text: You fly down… and a girl says: “Don't catch it! Look how it glows. Let it go free.” They watch you for a moment and you fly on.

n3.text: You land on the ground to rest and a toad comes closer. What do you do?

choices.text: Play dead and jump with a click!
Keep walking as if nothing happened

n4.text: Click! You flip into the air and land far away. The toad leaves. In the distance, two little green lights answer you.

e_learn.text: Whoa, close one! Click beetle fireflies are jumping beetles: when there's danger, they play dead and then flip away with a click. Try again.

e_happy.text: It was another firefly. Together you light up the night on the plains. People once used fireflies to light their way; today we have flashlights, and they can stay free.

stories.title: From the pond to the sky

n1.text: You're a dragonfly nymph living at the bottom of a pond. You don't have wings yet, but you do have a surprise jaw that shoots out like an arm.

choices.text: Wait quietly for a mosquito larva to swim by
Climb out onto the shore right now

n2.text: A mosquito larva swims by. Snap! You catch it with your jaw: that means fewer mosquitoes. Months go by and you grow by shedding your skin. One day you feel it's time…

choices.text: Climb a stem out of the water

n3.text: You grip the stem tightly. Your skin splits down the back and out comes… a dragonfly! Your wings are crumpled and soft. What do you do?

choices.text: Wait in the sun for them to dry

n4.text: Your wings shine now. Your old nymph skin stays on the stem, like an empty costume. Where do you fly?

choices.text: To catch mosquitoes over the pond

e_learn.text: It's not your time yet: your wings aren't ready. Dragonfly nymphs can spend months, even years!, underwater before coming out.

e_learn2.text: You can't fly with soft wings. Newly emerged dragonflies wait still for an hour or two until they harden. Patience is brave too!

e_happy.text: You're one of the best flyers in the world! You fly forward, backward and hover in midair. And you keep catching mosquitoes, now on the wing.
